overview: Monday's news is dominated by the US-Iran standoff and oil-market jitters, a smog emergency in Delhi after Diwali, a political fight over Parliament and the Election Commission, and the opening of the COP31 climate summit in Antalya.

items.headline: US and Iran quietly negotiate as Trump calls fresh strikes highly unlikely
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said new strikes on Iran are highly unlikely while nuclear negotiations continue, though he has not ruled them out. Oil prices fell on the signal of restraint.
items.detail: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the war on Iran is not necessarily popular but is needed to stop a nuclear threat, and he played down the chances of a quick breakthrough in talks, calling Tehran's demands unrealistic. Reports say the two sides are negotiating quietly even as shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz continue. UAE minister Anwar Gargash has warned of prolonged regional uncertainty and said a US-Iran settlement looks difficult.
items.analysis: The mix of public threats and private talks makes the next few weeks hard to read, and oil prices and Gulf travel are sensitive to every shift. Watch whether the shipping attacks stop, since that would be a clearer sign of progress than statements.

items.headline: Delhi air turns 'severe' the morning after Diwali as smog spreads
items.summary: Parts of Delhi crossed into the 'severe' air quality category on Monday, a day after Diwali, with grey haze over the city. Smog was also reported in Mumbai and Chennai.
items.detail: The Times of India reported that the smog was near the severe level after a firecracker ban was widely defied during the festival. The BJP has blamed years of policy failure and alleged a conspiracy, while AAP and Congress have questioned the AQI data. The Supreme Court has asked Delhi and three states for an action plan on vehicular pollution.
items.analysis: Winter smog in north India is a recurring problem driven by crop-residue burning, traffic and weather, and the Diwali spike makes it visible again. The political argument over the data is as important as the air itself, since trust in the numbers affects what governments do next.

items.headline: President taps Gadi Eisenkot to try to form Israel's next government
items.summary: Israel's president has asked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a government, a setback for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Eisenkot has said Netanyahu's party is welcome to join a government he leads.
items.detail: Reports describe the move as a setback for Netanyahu, whose position has weakened. Eisenkot has said he is open to Netanyahu's party joining his coalition, which signals a possible power-sharing arrangement. NDTV reported that he faces tough odds in building a coalition.
items.analysis: Forming a government in Israel requires a majority in parliament, so the outcome depends on which parties agree to join. The result would matter for regional diplomacy, including talks on Iran and the Gulf.

items.headline: Bangladesh's ousted leader Sheikh Hasina seeks a new passport
items.summary: Sheikh Hasina, who was ousted as Bangladesh's leader and now lives in exile, has applied for a new passport and identity card, a step that may signal a plan to return. Bangladesh's law minister has called her a convicted criminal.
items.detail: Reuters reported the passport request as the clearest sign yet of a possible return to Bangladesh. The Bangladeshi law minister said an extradition request has been sent to India, where Hasina is living. Her supporters and critics are likely to read the move very differently.
items.analysis: Extradition between neighbours is rarely simple and depends on diplomacy as well as courts. Watch whether India responds publicly to the extradition request.

items.headline: US Democrats push impeachment of Defence Secretary Hegseth after midterms
items.summary: Democrats have said they will press for impeachment of Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth after their midterm gains, and some Republicans have also turned against him. President Trump told CBS that his deportation policy was 'too tough'.
items.detail: Reports say the Democrats gave the White House an ultimatum to fire Hegseth or face impeachment proceedings, and that a top House Democrat is a firm yes on impeachment. Trump, in a CBS interview, said the immigration crackdown was too tough and that it played a part in the midterm defeat of his party. The Financial Times and other outlets are debating what Democrats should do next.
items.analysis: Impeachment in the US House needs only a simple majority, but removal requires a two-thirds Senate vote, which makes the outcome uncertain. The debate also shows how the midterm results are reshaping both parties' priorities.

items.headline: COP31 climate summit opens in Antalya amid geopolitical strain
items.summary: The UN climate summit COP31 opened in Antalya, Turkey, and runs from 9 to 20 November. Negotiators face geopolitical tensions, arguments over climate finance and warnings that the 1.5 degree goal is under strain.
items.detail: Reports say wars and rivalries are pulling governments toward protecting their own interests, which makes cooperation harder. India's climate team, led by minister Bhupendra Yadav, is preparing its diplomacy for the talks. Commentators have pointed to climate finance, meaning money for poorer countries to cut emissions and adapt, as a key sticking point.
items.analysis: COP summits usually end with incremental deals, and progress on finance is often the hardest part. Watch whether the summit produces firm commitments on money for developing countries.

items.headline: Gunman who killed six in Krakow dies in hospital; three bodies found at his home
items.summary: Police in Poland said the gunman who killed six people in Krakow has died in hospital. Three bodies were found at his house.
items.detail: Reports say the shooting in Krakow left six people dead, and the suspect later died in hospital. Police found three bodies at the suspect's home, linking the case to the house where he was staying. Authorities have not yet publicly set out a full motive in the headlines available.
items.analysis: Mass shootings in European cities prompt debate on gun laws and mental health services, but the investigation is still at an early stage. Further police findings will shape the picture.

items.headline: Train collision in Egypt near Cairo kills seven and injures more than 100
items.summary: Two trains collided near Cairo in Egypt, killing at least seven people and injuring more than 100, according to authorities.
items.detail: Al Jazeera, the BBC and CNN all reported the crash on Sunday, with the death toll given as seven. Rail accidents in Egypt have drawn attention in the past because of ageing infrastructure and safety concerns. Investigations usually look at signalling, human error and maintenance.
items.analysis: Official findings on the cause will matter for rail safety in Egypt. The toll may still rise, given the number of injured.

items.headline: Kharge's 'Eid of Happiness' Diwali greeting sparks BJP attack
items.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge described Diwali as the 'Eid of happiness' in his greeting, and the BJP has accused him of appeasement and of hurting Hindu sentiments.
items.detail: BJP leaders, including Bihar BJP chief Sanjay Saraogi, said the remark was aimed at winning votes, and one BJP statement questioned whether Congress would call Eid the 'Diwali of joy'. The BJP has also called Kharge a mouthpiece of the Gandhi family. The headlines do not give a detailed Congress reply, so the story is best read as a political exchange over identity and festival greetings.
items.analysis: Festival greetings often become political flashpoints ahead of elections. Both sides are using the exchange to frame their appeal to voters.

items.headline: Parliament's Monsoon session stays formally open for a record 88 days
items.summary: The Monsoon session of Parliament has remained unprorogued for 88 days, a record that breaks the 2008 mark. The House has not been formally closed even though it has been adjourned since August.
items.detail: Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi has listed 10 alleged poll irregularities and criticised the Centre and the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls and delimitation. Home Minister Amit Shah has offered a special session on SIR after Rahul Gandhi challenged Prime Minister Modi to an open debate. Prorogation is the formal step that ends a session, and it is usually done by the President on the government's advice.
items.analysis: The record length of an unprorogued session is largely symbolic, but it shows how stalled the House has been. Whether the government accepts a special session will be the next thing to watch.

items.headline: Supreme Court seeks responses on lifelong immunity for election commissioners
items.summary: The Supreme Court has asked for responses on a law that gives blanket, lifelong immunity to the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners. The INDIA bloc has announced a second phase of its campaign against the CEC.
items.detail: The petition challenges a legal provision that shields election commissioners from legal action for official acts, and the court has sought replies from the government. Opposition parties say the Election Commission needs more accountability, especially after controversies over the SIR. A former Chief Election Commissioner has said that the West Bengal election is not legally valid, a view that is disputed by the Election Commission and the Trinamool Congress according to the reports.
items.analysis: The case goes to the heart of how far independent constitutional bodies can be held to account. The government's reply and the court's direction will be closely watched.

items.headline: PM Modi warns of 'dimaagi Naxals' after Maoist decline in Bastar
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the Maoist movement has largely gone but that 'dimaagi Naxals' are still instigating people. Congress responded by accusing him of desperation.
items.detail: Modi made the remark while speaking to security forces during Diwali in Bastar, a former Maoist stronghold. The Congress party responded with a sharp attack, saying the government is pressing a narrative to hide its failures. The headlines do not give further detail on specific operations or figures.
items.analysis: Left-wing extremism has declined in recent years, but the debate over how to describe the remaining threat is political. The argument will continue as the government pushes its security agenda.

items.headline: Keralam begins petrol checks for excess ethanol after Karnataka findings
items.summary: Keralam has started inspecting fuel pumps and testing petrol samples for excess ethanol, after Karnataka reported high ethanol levels in some fuel. Testing is under way at select outlets across four districts.
items.detail: The state government ordered checks after Karnataka's findings on E20 petrol, which contains 20 per cent ethanol. Union Minister Suresh Gopi has said both states are free to test fuel and has warned against politicising the issue, while defending the E20 policy. The state is sending samples for laboratory testing, and the results will decide whether further action is needed.
items.analysis: The row is about fuel quality, consumer trust and the national push for ethanol blending. Lab results will be the main test of whether the concerns are real.

items.headline: Second phase of anti-drug drive Operation Toofan to start on 16 November
items.summary: Keralam will launch the second phase of its anti-drug drive, Operation Toofan, on 16 November, Ramesh Chennithala has said. Separately, the state's Home Minister has warned of strict action against drunk and erratic driving.
items.detail: The anti-drug campaign is the second phase of an earlier push against narcotics in the state. Police in Kochi seized three private buses after finding drivers allegedly drunk and recorded 35 offences in a special drive. The Chief Minister has promised strict action against reckless driving by private buses.
items.analysis: Enforcement drives like these tend to be judged by sustained follow-through rather than the initial launch. Watch for data on arrests and convictions after the November campaign begins.

items.headline: Court denies bail to two actors in Kochi doctor assault case
items.summary: A court in Kochi has denied bail to actors Athulya Chandra and Bibin Perumbilli, two days after their arrest, in a case involving an assault on a doctor.
items.detail: The case is connected to a doctor assault, and the police have also issued a lookout notice for a doctor booked in a separate rape case in Kochi. The headlines do not give further detail on the allegations, which remain before the courts. Bail decisions in such cases are often reviewed again at a higher court.
items.analysis: The case has drawn attention because of the profiles of those involved. The next steps will be decided by the courts, and the accused are entitled to the presumption of innocence.

items.headline: Great Nicobar airport land declaration deadline extended by one year
items.summary: The Andaman and Nicobar administration has extended by one year the statutory period for making the declaration needed to acquire land for the Great Nicobar airport project.
items.detail: A declaration is the formal notice that starts land acquisition, and the extension gives the administration more time to complete that step. The Great Nicobar project has been contested by environmental groups and others over forest loss and the rights of tribal communities on the islands. The headlines do not indicate new court rulings or clearances on the project.
items.analysis: The extension is procedural but keeps the project moving on paper. Attention will turn to the forest clearances and tribal consultations that remain.

items.headline: Proposed Western Ghats protection zone stuck as climate threats grow
items.summary: A proposed ecological protection zone for the Western Ghats faces growing climate threats even as its formal notification remains stalled.
items.detail: The Western Ghats is a mountain range along India's west coast, known for its biodiversity and for frequent landslides and floods. A proposed protection zone has been discussed for years, but it has not yet been notified in final form. Down To Earth reports that climate pressures are increasing while the decision remains pending.
items.analysis: Delay in notifying the zone means the protective framework is still not fully in place as extreme weather becomes more common. Watch for any movement on the final notification.

items.headline: El Nino is here, and warnings say India's farmers need more support
items.summary: An El Nino pattern has developed this year, and commentary says the early warning must reach farmers who lack institutional support.
items.detail: The Times of India says El Nino is here and asks how ready farmers are. Mongabay India notes that El Nino years usually weaken the Indian monsoon, though the link is a tendency rather than a rule, and that this year's signal from the India Meteorological Department was unusually emphatic. The commentary argues that small and marginal farmers often miss forecasts and advice.
items.analysis: El Nino affects rainfall, crop planning and food prices, so the readiness of farmers matters for the year ahead. The gap between official forecasts and what reaches the field is the key question.

items.headline: LIC and brokers push back on IRDAI's proposed commission reforms
items.summary: LIC has said it expects limited impact from IRDAI's proposed commission reforms, while brokers have asked the government to intervene against the distribution changes.
items.detail: IRDAI, India's insurance regulator, has proposed changes to how commissions are paid to agents and intermediaries. LIC says its lower expense ratio and distribution structure should protect it, and it expects higher-cost insurers to feel more pressure. Brokers have met Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and PMO officials to seek changes to the proposals.
items.analysis: Commission rules shape how policies are sold and how much they cost customers, so the outcome will matter for the whole sector. Watch for the final regulation and whether it is revised after industry feedback.

items.headline: Insurers may boost medical tourism by covering treatment for foreign patients
items.summary: Industry voices say global insurance cover for foreign patients could sharply increase medical tourism to India, with Apollo Hospitals' Sangita Reddy among those making the case.
items.detail: Apollo Hospitals has said that broader insurance access for international patients could help the growth of medical tourism in India. Business Standard reported that numbers could rise steeply once insurers begin covering treatment for foreign patients coming to India. Asia Insurance Review also argues that global health insurers can give a boost to the sector.
items.analysis: International patients are a growing market for Indian hospitals, but insurance acceptance is a major hurdle. Whether global insurers add India to their networks will shape the trend.

items.headline: Aon creates North American healthcare unit under Nick Gaudiosi
items.summary: Broker Aon has set up a North American healthcare unit led by Nick Gaudiosi, a move that reflects growing focus on health benefits and risk.
items.detail: Reinsurance News reported the new unit on 6 November. Large brokers create specialist units when a sector grows in size and complexity, and healthcare cover in the US is a large and costly market. The headlines do not give details of the unit's size or revenue targets.
items.analysis: Specialist units are a sign that brokers see health cover as a major growth area. The unit's client wins and results will show whether the strategy works.

items.headline: Drone attack injures four at Dubai Airport as Gulf tensions rise
items.summary: A drone attack injured four people at Dubai Airport, according to reports tied to Iran's escalation of operations in the Gulf.
items.detail: DD News reported the drone attack on Dubai Airport, linking it to wider Gulf security concerns. A Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh was reportedly damaged in a separate attempted attack. UAE minister Anwar Gargash has warned that regional uncertainty may last for a long time, and that a US-Iran settlement appears difficult.
items.analysis: Attacks on major travel hubs affect the daily life of residents and visitors. Watch for airport and airline security announcements in the coming days.

items.headline: Airlines suspend Saudi routes until 19 November, flight cancellations continue
items.summary: UAE flight cancellations are continuing, with airlines suspending routes to Saudi Arabia until 19 November.
items.detail: The Economic Times reported that the suspensions are part of wider flight disruption in the region. Gulf airspace closures have also pushed Middle Eastern airlines toward large losses this year, according to Avi-Go. Travellers are advised to check their airline's latest notices before departure.
items.analysis: Flight disruption is one of the most visible effects of the regional conflict for residents and businesses in the UAE. The end date of 19 November may change depending on developments.

items.headline: UAE temperatures dip on Tuesday, with rain possible in eastern and coastal areas
items.summary: Temperatures in the UAE are forecast to dip on Tuesday, with heavy rain possible in eastern and coastal areas.
items.detail: Emirates 24|7 reported the forecast for Tuesday. Heavy rain in the east and along the coast can cause temporary road disruption and waterlogging, so people are advised to check local updates. The change follows a warm autumn across the region.
items.analysis: Short bursts of heavy rain are unusual but can affect driving and outdoor plans. Official alerts from the UAE National Center of Meteorology are the most reliable guide.

items.headline: Sensex and Nifty slip after a seven-day rally as profit-taking sets in
items.summary: Indian stocks opened lower on Monday after a seven-day rally, with the Sensex down about 94 points in early trade and the Nifty below 24,950.
items.detail: The Diwali Muhurat session on Sunday ended marginally lower, snapping the rally. IT stocks such as HCL Tech and Infosys dragged the indices, while banking shares offered some support. Analysts said the pre-Diwali run-up had cooled off, and that the market had posted its longest winning streak in three years in the previous week.
items.analysis: Profit-taking after a long rally is normal, and the early moves are not a clear trend. Global tech sentiment and oil prices are the main outside factors to watch.

items.headline: Rupee rises to a seven-month high as crude eases
items.summary: The rupee gained about 24 paise to around 93.74 against the US dollar in early trade, its strongest level in about seven months.
items.detail: Reuters reported that the rupee's rally has put the RBI's dollar-buying threshold in focus. The Hindu and others said the gains came as crude oil prices eased and foreign inflows improved. Moneycontrol quoted analysts who expect the rupee at around 92.5 per dollar by the end of December, though the currency had earlier hit record lows.
items.analysis: A weaker rupee makes oil imports more expensive, so currency moves matter for inflation and the import bill. Central bank action will be watched if the currency swings sharply.

items.headline: Oil falls below $100 as Trump signals restraint on Iran; gold rises
items.summary: Brent crude slipped below $100 a barrel as Trump signalled restraint on Iran, and gold climbed above $4,120.
items.detail: Oil prices fell on hopes that the US-Iran standoff will not escalate, even as shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz continue. Gold rose as the dollar softened and inflation worries eased. Greek shipowners have made large gains from tanker sales as the conflict has lifted charter rates, according to iMarine.
items.analysis: Oil and gold are both reacting to geopolitical headlines, so prices can reverse quickly. The Strait of Hormuz remains the key risk for energy markets.

items.headline: Asian stocks bounce after AI-led selloff, Nvidia probe weighs on tech
items.summary: Asian stock markets recovered from an earlier tech rout as Mideast jitters eased, though the dollar remained firm on bets about the US Federal Reserve.
items.detail: Reuters and Al Jazeera reported the rebound, while Nvidia faced an investigation into the relationship of its chief executive with a suspected Chinese spy. US payrolls rose by 165,000 in October, and markets now bet that the Fed could restart rate hikes in December. Bloomberg also reported that Alphabet is considering an Asian bond sale amid AI-related volatility.
items.analysis: Global equities are sensitive to both AI sentiment and US interest-rate expectations. A surprise from the Fed or fresh news on Nvidia could reset the mood quickly.

items.headline: Nvidia opens investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's ties to alleged Chinese spy
items.summary: Nvidia has opened an investigation into Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese executive accused of spying, according to The New York Times.
items.detail: The New York Times reported that Nvidia's board is examining the matter, and NDTV reported that Huang admitted to a past relationship with the executive. Alice Huang is accused of gathering secrets, and reports say the case involves a Singapore firm. Nvidia's board has issued a statement, and the investigation is ongoing.
items.analysis: The story touches on export controls, corporate governance and China-US tech rivalry, and it could affect how investors view the world's most valuable AI chip company. The facts are still emerging, so caution is warranted.

items.headline: UK public bodies struggle with a flood of chatbot-written complaints
items.summary: British public bodies say they are battling an onslaught of complaints generated by chatbots, which is adding to their workload.
items.detail: The Guardian reported that the problem, which it called 'AI clog', is affecting bodies that handle complaints and applications. AI tools can produce long and polished complaints quickly, which can make it harder for staff to find genuine cases. The story reflects a wider question about how institutions adapt to cheap automated writing.
items.analysis: The case shows a practical downside of generative AI: it can lower the cost of producing documents while raising the cost of handling them. Institutions may need new triage tools.

items.headline: India's GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission documented as Indian space sector grows
items.summary: The government has published a note on the GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission, part of a wider push to build India's space capacity.
items.detail: The pib.gov.in release covers the GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission, and other government notes this week describe India's space sovereignty goals. The NVS series is a set of navigation satellites for India's regional positioning system, NavIC. A separate Times of India piece argues that the sector will not wait for those who fall behind.
items.analysis: Regional navigation satellites reduce reliance on foreign systems for positioning and timing. Details of the mission's outcome are not in the headlines available.

items.headline: India becomes the world's third-largest startup ecosystem
items.summary: India has been ranked as the world's third-largest startup ecosystem, with reports saying it has created over 2.3 million jobs.
items.detail: News On AIR and NKTV both reported the ranking, and BW Disrupt has asked why India's best startups often get stuck in the middle, as they scale. Industry commentators say funding for growth-stage companies is the main gap. The headlines do not give the full methodology behind the ranking.
items.analysis: Rankings depend heavily on the methodology used, so the headline figure should be read with care. The bigger test is whether startups move from early stage to large, profitable companies.

items.headline: Hydrogen storage in salt caverns passes leak test; Hyundai and Air Liquide expand hydrogen trucks in China
items.summary: EWE has completed a leak test at a salt-cavern hydrogen storage facility converted from natural gas, and Hyundai's HTWO has teamed with Air Liquide to expand hydrogen mobility in China.
items.detail: Storing hydrogen underground in salt caverns is one of the few ways to hold large volumes for long periods, which is needed for grid balancing. Converting an old gas cavern saves time and money, but the key test is whether the cavern holds gas without leaking. In China, the HTWO partnership with Air Liquide targets the hydrogen commercial vehicle supply chain, including fuelling and gas supply.
items.analysis: Hydrogen only helps the energy transition if it can be stored safely and cheaply, so leak tests are a key milestone. Commercial vehicle deals show where demand may come from first.

items.headline: Surface defects speed up methane reforming in ruthenium-ceria catalysts
items.summary: A study reports that surface defects in ruthenium-ceria catalysts can enhance methane reforming, a reaction that turns methane into hydrogen and carbon monoxide.
items.detail: Methane reforming is a well-established industrial route to hydrogen, and catalysts speed up the reaction. Ceria is a cerium oxide that often supports metal catalysts and can hold oxygen in its surface. The finding suggests that engineering defects on the surface could improve how well the catalyst works.
items.analysis: Better catalysts can lower the energy and cost of hydrogen production from methane, and the lessons may carry over to cleaner routes. The headline work is still a laboratory-scale result.

items.headline: AI helps find nitrogen impurities that poison catalysts in waste plastic oil
items.summary: Researchers have used AI to identify nitrogen-based impurities that poison catalysts when waste plastic is converted into oil through pyrolysis.
items.detail: Pyrolysis heats plastic without oxygen to break it into oil and gas, which can then be turned into fuels or chemicals. Impurities in the oil can deactivate the catalysts that upgrade it, which slows the whole recycling process. Reports from several outlets say the AI analysis pinpointed the specific nitrogen compounds responsible.
items.analysis: Identifying the exact poisons is a practical step toward making chemical recycling of plastics more reliable. Industrial results will depend on whether the fix can be applied at scale.

items.headline: arXiv: honest error bars for machine-learned atomic force models
items.summary: A new arXiv preprint proposes a way to give calibrated uncertainty estimates for machine-learned interatomic potentials, the models used to simulate how atoms move and bond.
items.detail: Machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on quantum calculations and then used to run large simulations quickly. The authors note that the standard Bayesian error bars often understate real errors because the model is not a perfect match for the physics. Their method, a delete-one-configuration jackknife, re-fits the model many times with each training example left out to measure how much its predictions vary, and they test the approach on silicon against Bayesian and other baselines.
items.analysis: Reliable error bars tell researchers when a simulation can be trusted, which matters for materials design. The result is a preprint and has not yet been peer reviewed.

items.headline: arXiv: designing crystals by nudging a pretrained foundation model
items.summary: A new arXiv preprint introduces DEFEAT, a method that makes a pretrained atomic foundation model differentiable so that its predictions can guide the design of superconductors and semiconductors.
items.detail: Designing a crystal usually means choosing elements, their ratios and their arrangement, but computers can only take gradient steps on continuous variables such as atomic positions. The authors' method allows the model to propagate gradients through the composition as well, which lets a search adjust both elements and structure toward a target property. The approach builds on a large pretrained model called EquiformerV3.
items.analysis: Inverse design could shorten the search for new materials, but predictions still need experimental checks. Readers may want to see whether the method finds materials that can be synthesised.

items.headline: Panama's winter cold-water upwelling nearly failed in 2025
items.summary: Every winter for at least 40 years, cold water has risen off Panama's Pacific coast, but in 2025 it almost did not appear.
items.detail: A report from Futura says the cold water, known as upwelling, has been a regular winter feature off Panama's Pacific coast for at least four decades. In 2025 it almost failed to arrive at all. Upwelling happens when winds push warm surface water away from the coast, letting cooler, nutrient-rich water rise from below, which supports marine food chains and fishing. The headline does not give the cause of the 2025 shortfall, but the weakening of this process is a concern for scientists tracking changes in the Pacific.
items.analysis: A seasonal ocean process that has been reliable for decades can change quickly, which matters for fisheries that depend on it. Watch whether this was a one-year dip or the start of a longer trend.

sources.name: Futura, le média qui explore le monde

items.headline: Streetlights cut crime, but the effect may not last
items.summary: A new study finds that streetlights reduce crime, but the benefit does not hold up over the long term.
items.detail: A report in Governing covers a study finding that adding or improving streetlights is linked to lower crime. The same study found the effect fades over time rather than lasting. Better lighting is a common low-cost tool that cities use to try to make public spaces safer, often alongside policing and community programmes. The headline does not give specific figures or the study's methods, so the scale of the drop and how quickly it fades are not clear from this summary.
items.analysis: Short-term gains from cheap measures can be appealing to local governments, so the finding that they fade is useful for planning. Watch for follow-up research on whether lighting works better when combined with other measures.

items.headline: Captive-bred great Indian bustards released in Rajasthan, with a setback
items.summary: Four captive-bred great Indian bustards were released into the wild in Rajasthan in early October, but one was found dead on October 17.
items.detail: Mongabay India reports that four captive-bred great Indian bustards were released in early October at Desert National Park in Rajasthan, a step described as a milestone for Project Great Indian Bustard. On October 17, one of the four birds was found dead, apparently killed by a predator. Two losses have been recorded this year, yet authorities say the rewilding effort is on track. The great Indian bustard is a large ground-nesting bird that is critically endangered, and captive breeding followed by release is one of several methods used to rebuild wild populations.
items.analysis: Authorities and conservationists judge success over years, not weeks, so the survival of the remaining birds in the coming months will be an important signal. Watch for updates on how the released birds are doing.
